content: Visit note | 2025-03-22 10:30 AM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Abdul Sheikh, 20, male. Mr. Sheikh attends today because of a painful red lump at the edge of his eyelid, and the lid around it has become swollen over the past two days. He is a software developer and the lump appeared during a stressful week at work in Keraniganj, when he was sleeping poorly and rubbing his eye often. He says the lump is tender to touch and the eye waters a little, but his vision is unaffected. He has no other medical conditions. He has not used any eye drops or ointments, and he has not had a similar lump before. He denies fever, discharge from the eye, or reduced vision. He also denies headache or pain elsewhere. On examination, there is a small tender swelling at the margin of the upper lid with mild lid swelling, and the eye itself is quiet. On examination: lump about 4 mm on the right upper eyelid, BP 112/77 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 88 kg. The cornea is clear and the conjunctiva is only mildly red. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a warm compress four times a day, not to squeeze the lump, and to avoid eye makeup. Follow-up in 1 week.
